subtitle: Galaxies from the first moments
yt_title: The Oldest Galaxy Ever Found 🔭 | Ep. 24 #shorts
description:
Episode 24 of a daily journey through the universe. 🔭
We look through the James Webb Space Telescope: a 6.5-meter mirror 1.5 million km away, galaxies whose light traveled 13 billion years, and MoM-z14, the most distant galaxy ever confirmed.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 25: Next stop, the edge of the observable universe.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #webbdeepfield #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode twenty-four. Next stop... the dawn of time.
This is the James Webb Space Telescope. Its mirror is six and a half meters wide, and it works a million and a half kilometers from Earth.
segments.headline: 1.5 million km from Earth

segments.text: Every dot of light here is a galaxy. Some of this light traveled more than thirteen billion years to reach us.
segments.headline: Every dot is a galaxy

segments.text: In twenty twenty-five, Webb confirmed the most distant galaxy ever seen. We see it as it was just two hundred eighty million years after the Big Bang.
That's when the universe was only about two percent of its current age.
These early galaxies are bigger and brighter than scientists expected. Webb is rewriting the story of the first galaxies.
segments.headline: Bigger than expected

segments.text: Tomorrow, we reach the end of everything we can see. Next stop: the edge of the observable universe. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-five.
